title: Audit of c29's label-free kernel-drive C:swim-divide: S, I, B, D and swim-then-divide lineages replicate on new seeds 5-6 and at dt/2; M is crowd-dependent autochemotaxis: an isolated cell does not swim
summary: Construction: division and the ring are not imposed (no division rule; L is made only by the inside catalyst and pushed to the wall by the chi drift, so the ring passes the L3 clause; chi=0 loses it). Motion comes from a written chemotactic advection of all matter, v = mu G*(phi^2 grad S)/G*(phi^2), so M needs gradients made by consumption. Replication: seed 5 (labkit) gives L rim/core 1.56, 235 persistent splits, gen 6, jamming by t~6000; the same seed at the world's own dt=0.5 gives 1.55, 225, gen 6. My tracker (align.py) finds 40 and 42 tracks >= 3 BL (2 sqrt(A/pi)) on seeds 5 and 6, and 2 lineages per seed that swim >= 3 BL and then split into two persistent daughters. Deciding control for M: 3 median cells taken at t=2400 and transplanted alone into a fresh bath do not swim (<= 0.83 BL); they grow 25-28x and split. In situ, swimmers follow the local S gradient (cos 0.66-0.68 at 12 px) far more than the colony-scale gradient (0.30-0.36 at 48 px), with a bias away from neighbours (0.34-0.41 within 40 px). So swimming is real and not a global-gradient drift, but it is collective autochemotaxis that exists only in a crowd during colonization.

verdicts.limitation: M is collective: a lone cell in a fed bath does not break symmetry and swim; motion exists only while a crowd colonizes depleted substrate, and stops when the torus jams (t~6000, t~7500 at dt/2). The motility law itself (advection of phi, K and L at mu times the kernel-averaged substrate gradient, clipped at vmax 0.4) is written into the model, not derived from forces. The claim's ringtrack divides net displacement by sqrt(A), not 2 sqrt(A/pi): its BL figures are 13% high (#333 5.07 -> 4.5 diameters; #177 3.56 -> 3.2); they still pass. I did not re-score the ring on the specific swim-then-divide lineages (population ring only). Swim-then-divide lineages are rare: 2 of ~40 swimmers per seed.
